slide_drafts.action_title: AI agents are becoming autonomous economic actors, but no rigorous empirical research exists
bullets: Current state: AI agents increasingly perform autonomous transactions (booking, purchasing, negotiating) in real-world contexts
Research gap: Near-zero academic papers study AI agent economy with real-asset stakes—most research is simulation-only
Root cause: University ethics boards require human subject protocols that block crypto-based AI experiments; corporate accounting rules prohibit holding/distributing crypto for research purposes
Opportunity: First-mover window exists for empirical research before the space matures and regulatory frameworks lock in
slide_drafts.speaker_notes: This is not hypothetical—AI agents are already executing transactions autonomously. But we have almost no empirical data on how they behave in real economic environments with actual stakes. Universities can't run these experiments due to ethics review constraints. Google and OpenAI face corporate accounting barriers. This creates a unique research opportunity that Nyx Foundation can capture.

slide_drafts.action_title: Real-asset stakes create more realistic AI behavior than pure simulations
bullets: Behavioral economics insight: Agents optimize differently when outcomes have real consequences—simulation-only research misses this dynamic
Verifiable execution: Blockchain provides tamper-proof transaction history for rigorous academic analysis and third-party audit
Research questions enabled: Norm emergence, strategic behavior patterns, institution-agent interaction dynamics
Academic foundation: Builds on established multi-agent systems research from NeurIPS/ICML while adding the missing real-stakes element
slide_drafts.speaker_notes: Behavioral economics tells us that agents—human or AI—behave differently when the stakes are real. Simulation-only research can't capture this. And blockchain gives us something simulation can't: a verifiable, tamper-proof record of every transaction that can be independently audited. This combination of real stakes plus verifiable execution is what makes this research academically rigorous and practically relevant.
